alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change in the last rollout we see a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit_rate for long sequences (8k windows) on the gtx-pool. Profiling shows fewer exact-key hits, more partial KV lookups.
julia: Link to the panel? can you paste the query + the stack trace for the hot path? :eyes:
alex: dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prefix_cache/explorer?panel=hit_rate_by_model_route_customer
Also paste from pprof: ```flat profile:  42.3% fused_attention_kernel, 18.7% kv_lookup, 9.5% batching.dispatch``` — looks like fused kernel now dominates and batches are smaller at dispatch.
tony: that matches my PR (789): I changed the batching heuristic to prefer lower latency sub-batches when fused kernels are available. The idea was to reduce tail latency but I didn't expect it to affect key alignment so much.
maya: quick join — here's the SQL we use for hit_rate:
```
SELECT model, route, customer, count_if(hit)/count(*) AS hit_rate, sum(tokens_saved) as tokens_saved
FROM prefix_cache.events
WHERE ts BETWEEN $__start AND $__end
GROUP BY model, route, customer
ORDER BY tokens_saved DESC
```
we can add `batch_size_bucket` and `kernel_variant` to slice.
sam: hypothesis: smaller sub-batches + kernel fusion changes the order/packing of requests so the prefix-key hashing distribution is altered (hash collisions + sequence alignment). meaning identical prefixes end up in different batch windows => cache miss more often. Quick experiment: run a synthetic workload that emits identical 1k prefixes at randomized inter-arrival and compare hit_rate when batching heuristic is old vs new.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2955551000 by tony to staging succeeded (commit: 7c3a2f). Health checks: ok. :white_check_mark:
julia: can we add a dashboard panel that correlates kernel_variant + batch_size_bucket with hit_rate and tokens_saved per-customer? want to quickly identify high-impact tenants.
alex: yes — propose three new panels: 1) heatmap: hit_rate by model x kernel_variant (time series), 2) waterfall: tokens_saved delta (pre vs post) by customer, 3) scatter: avg_batch_size vs hit_rate per-route. Also add an alert when customer tokens_saved decreases >15% over 6h.
tony: I'll revert the heuristic in staging and run the synthetic at 10k qps. Also will add instrumentation to tag the request with `batch_boundary_id` so we can trace key alignment across batches.
maya: I'll add `kernel_variant` and `batch_boundary_id` to the prefix_cache.events schema (append-only tags) and update the grafana queries. also adding a quick aggregated metric `hit_alignment` = count_exact_matches / count_total to measure alignment directly.
sam: timeline: revert + synthetic by EOD, dashboards updated by tomorrow AM. if the revert restores hit_rate, we can iterate a hybrid heuristic that biases batching only for short sequences.
alex: sounds good — owners: tony (revert + synthetic), maya (schema + dashboards), julia (alert thresholds + ops runbook). I'll post a short incident note if we cross the 10% tokens_saved regression for any top-10 tenant.
